title: Play & Capture — phone portrait (compact width)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
Live region: 'Captured 8 bars at 92 BPM into layer 2. Looping.'
a: Sketch menu: library, rename, save state, export. One sketch = one shared tempo/meter + its parts (first slice: one part; four is a milestone, not a max).
Grid chip shows the inferred grid (tempo · meter). Tap = re-open grid review. Never changes playback speed.
Undo is always visible (48dp). Label read aloud: 'Undo Capture layer 2'.
Input chip: device name + 'receiving' only after a real message arrived. Shape: filled dot = live, ring = connected-silent, ✕ = none.
Audio chip: 'Sound on' / 'Tap to start sound' / 'Interrupted – tap to resume'. Text + icon, not colour alone.
History chip: how much recent playing Capture can reach (proposed 120 s rolling + hard event/byte cap). Shows 'gap' if events were dropped under overload. No arming.
Sound pill targets the selected layer. ◀ ▶ step sounds while you keep playing; centre opens the Sound browser sheet.
Ribbon = the buffer made visible: what Capture will take. Dashed bracket previews the likely phrase so the result is predictable.
Layer strip: ◎ marks the capture target (text 'next', ring shape). Tap any layer to retarget. Long-press → layer actions.
Transport is secondary: capture never needs Play first. Click (metronome) is opt-in.
Capture: 112dp (proposed) tall, full width, bottom-centre. Optionally mapped to any spare CC/button/pad (no spare pedal required); sustain and playing keys are never taken by default.
Touch keys open as a drawer. Always labelled 'on screen' and never appear in the MIDI device list.

title: Play & Capture — phone landscape (compact height)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
a: Landscape: Capture becomes a tall right-hand rail (192×236dp) under the thumb; ribbon keeps the width.
Height < 480dp (compact height): status collapses into one 44dp row; no bottom sheets taller than 60% of height.
Layer strip moves to the bottom-left so hands on the controller never reach across the screen.

title: Fold folded / cover screen (narrow compact)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
a: Below 360dp wide the 4-chip layer strip collapses into one 'Target' chip (opens a 4-row picker). Capture keeps full height.
Status chips merge into one row; tapping it opens the full readiness panel.
Folding/unfolding must not stop sound, close the review, or drop the selection (window size classes change at runtime).

title: Fold open (medium width, flat) — Play + Layers side by side
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
a: Medium width (600–840dp): two panes. Layers are always visible, so retargeting capture is one tap with no navigation.
Each layer row 112dp: name, sound, length, note thumbnail, Mute/Solo with letters (not colour) and pressed state.
Capture stays in the Play pane at the bottom of the left half, inside the natural reach of the hand nearest the keyboard.

title: Fold half-open, tabletop posture (horizontal hinge)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
a: Tabletop (HALF_OPENED + horizontal fold): top half shows; bottom half takes all touch controls, like the media-player tabletop pattern.
Nothing interactive inside the fold bounds when isSeparating is true; layout re-flows when the posture changes.

title: Desktop browser (expanded / large width) — three regions
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
Touch keys (on screen) — or computer keys A–K when enabled
a: Expanded/large: layers left, play/edit centre, inspector right (sound, review, controller). Nothing is hidden behind sheets.
Every touch action has a key: C capture, Space play, ⌘Z undo, 1–4 target layer, E/D/R tools, ⌘K sounds. Shown in tooltips.
Web: chip names the transport ('Web MIDI'). Unsupported/denied browsers show the reason here, never a fake 'connected'.

title: First run — connect sound + keyboard (readiness)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
One tap starts audio, then asks for MIDI.
Not yet heard — play any key to test
Play the on-screen touch keys instead.
They are a touch instrument, not a MIDI device.
Start playing enables once Sound is on (keyboard optional).
a: Web: one explicit enable gesture resumes audio and then requests MIDI. The browser's own prompt varies by browser/state, so the touch count is not fixed. Native: auto-starts.
Connected ≠ receiving. The card only says 'Receiving ✓ C4 vel 72' after a real Note On arrives (proves the cable, channel, and permission).
Touch keys are offered as an equal path, labelled as on-screen; choosing them never marks the MIDI card ready.
One primary action per card; the final CTA is plain once sound is on. Order: sound first, so the first key press is heard.

a: Every state: title says what happened, line 2 says what is still safe, button says the next action. Icon + text, never colour alone.
Denied permission cannot be re-prompted by script once blocked by policy; the card gives the manual route instead of a dead button.
Audio paused: Capture continues only while MIDI delivery continues (A1). Hidden tab / background: delivery not guaranteed; on return, gaps are flagged.

title: Capture review & grid corrections (sheet over Play, loop keeps playing)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
(Play screen dimmed but live — keys still play)
Your timing is unchanged — only the grid moves.
a: Sheet is non-blocking: the loop keeps playing and the controller keeps sounding. Undo reverts the capture. For later layers the tempo is locked to the sketch.
Notes played before the loop start stay in the take (greyed, dashed). Moving the loop brings them back — nothing is cropped.
Loop length chips re-map bars; never stretch audio or notes. Selected chip has ✓ + filled shape.
Beat one: step by beat, or tap any note in the mini-timeline to make it '1'. Moves bar lines, not notes.

'Count it as': inferred tempo plus ½ / ×2 / manual controls, always shown. Extra alternatives only when inference justifies them; no confidence %. Meter 4/4 at first. Re-maps bars; never speeds playback.
Original take = hear the raw, unlooped performance exactly as played. Always one tap away, in review and later from the layer menu.
Keep is the default: dismissing the sheet, playing on, or capturing again keeps it. Discard is explicit and undoable.

title: Sound browser (sheet) — audition by playing
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
Play your keyboard to try a sound — it loads instantly.
a: Audition is playing: tapping a row loads it on the target layer while you keep playing. No separate preview mode to forget.
Categories are large chips (48dp, proposed); search for names. Sound names are PLACEHOLDERS until the sound set is chosen — no asset is promised.
Favourite star is its own 48dp target, separated from the row action by 8dp; state read as 'Favourite, on'.
Every sound change is one undo step ('Back to previous'). Controller ◀ ▶ sound steps are learnable.

title: Four-layer overview — phone portrait
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
Capture goes here next if 2 is full
a: The grid belongs to the sketch (set by the first capture). 'Review grid' re-opens corrections; notes never move.
Selected/target layer: thick outline + ◎ + text 'capture target'. Tap the row body to retarget; no colour-only state.
Muted: dashed outline, hollow notes, the word MUTED, and M shown pressed. Screen reader: 'Layer 3, Pad, muted'.
Empty layer explains what will happen. Four parts is a milestone, not a max; the first slice ships one part. All full → Capture asks (never replaces).

title: Touch piano roll — phone (edit tool, chord selected, dragging with loupe)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
a: Explicit tools with text labels. Current tool shown 3 ways: pressed chip, subtitle text, and grid hint. Delete/duplicate are actions, not modes.
Overview strip: 1-finger drag pans; the box is the visible window. Rulers: drag time ruler = pan time; drag keys = pan pitch.
Loop brace handles [ ] are 48dp hit targets on the time ruler; they snap to beats and edit the loop, never notes.
Loupe appears 96dp above the finger during any drag (flips below near the top edge): ×2.5 view + pitch · position · length readout.
Selected notes: thick outline + side handle tabs (outside short notes so they stay ≥48dp to hit) + count in action bar.
Velocity lane: stem height (not colour) shows velocity; selected notes' stems are bold. Drag a stem, or use 'Vel ±' stepper.
Action bar works on the selection — every drag has a tap alternative (Len ±, nudge by arrows in the overflow, Vel ±).

title: Piano roll interaction states (selection, resize, marquee, range, draw, ambiguity)
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
tap note = select; drag empty = marquee
dashed box; notes inside get outline
Duplicate range · Delete range · Loop to range
tap empty = add (last length); tap note = select
a: States are visually distinct without colour: outline weight, handles, dashed ghosts and on-canvas text.
Ghost (dashed) shows the pre-edit state until release; release commits one undo step; 2nd finger or drag back to origin cancels.
Hit-testing picks the nearest note centre within 24dp; if two candidates are within 8dp of each other, a picker appears instead of guessing.

title: Controller learn — map a pedal/button to Capture
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
Hands stay on the keys: map the actions you use most.
Press a button, pad or pedal. 10 s left.
CC 64 is usually your sustain pedal; mapping it
to Undo stops it sustaining. Press another control?
a: Learnable actions are a short list (not every control). Each row says its current mapping in words.
Learn shows live incoming messages so you can see the controller works; it times out after 10 s and cancels cleanly.
Defaults never take over sustain (CC 64) or playable keys. An optional command zone is off unless you enable it. Conflicts explained before overwriting.

title: Save, recovery and export
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
restored from 2 min ago (4 layers, 3 edits).
Both versions are kept until you choose.
Your sketch is safe while Blocks stays open.
Saving… / Not saved – retrying in 5 s
Stems share start + one length; tail follows the sound's release.
a: Recovery never silently picks: restored vs last-saved are both offered, and both are kept until one is chosen.
Save failure is a persistent banner (not a toast) with Retry and an escape hatch: export.
Export: MIDI + aligned stems (stems = later milestone). Length visible/changeable. Raw CC64/bend/pressure kept; synthetic note-offs not exported.

Max depth 2 from Play. Sheets keep the loop and the keyboard live; only the piano roll takes the full screen.
a: Hierarchy: Capture > what you're hearing (layers/sound) > repair. Settings never interrupt playing.

title: Capture edge states — no pulse, capture while playing, overload gap, all layers full
p: PROPOSED · not implemented · sizes are proposals pending measurement
½ / ×2 apply once a tempo is set.
Takes the last 4 bars you have played,
ending at the last bar line already passed.
Held note: released at loop end for
Joins at next loop start · 2.1 s
Input overload: Blocks could not keep
Nothing is merged or replaced silently.
a: 'No pulse' is a valid result: keep a free-time loop of the phrase, or set a tempo manually. No fabricated alternatives or confidence numbers.
While playing: selects only bounded history already played on the existing transport — never future notes or a bar line not yet reached.
Queued join: the new layer starts at the next loop boundary. Held/active notes get synthetic releases for playback only, stored apart from raw events.
Overload is a different state from normal age eviction: gaps/drops are flagged in the ribbon, the review and the take. Capture may fail or be partial; the UI never promises otherwise.
All slots full → an explicit choice. Default target is always an empty/new layer; never a silent destructive replace or merge.
